description: Measures the branch-weight structure of the atom H_n(q) element. The weights are a CONVEX combination at every A tested, so tr_M of the atom is bounded by the largest branch trace -- which, under the volume-conjecture correspondence the framework invokes, caps any effective volume by the largest BRANCH volume. That is the invariant which prunes 2^(2A+1) hyperbolicity questions to one max. Computes NO volumes: SnapPy is unavailable here.

the_bound.identity: atom = sum_b w_b rho(beta_b), tr_M linear
the_bound.measured: sum_b |w_b| = 1 and every w_b > 0 -- a convex combination
the_bound.under_volume_conjecture: Vol_eff(atom) <= max_b Vol(K_b) + log(sum_b |w_b|), and convexity kills the second term
the_bound.why_it_matters: turns 2^(2A+1) separate hyperbolicity questions into ONE: is any branch hyperbolic?

corrects_the_2A_plus_1_docstring.says: There are 2A + 1 such non-braid letters (two per nucleon, from its two ud pairs, plus one per interface).
corrects_the_2A_plus_1_docstring.measured: holds at A = 2 (5) and A = 4 (9); FAILS at A = 1, where the count is 2, not 3 -- a single nucleon has no interface, so the '+1' has nothing to count.
corrects_the_2A_plus_1_docstring.my_own_probe_too: atom_word_braid_letter_census_probe.py asserts the identity only over 2H/3He/4He, all A >= 2, so its assertion is true as tested but its framing implies a generality it never checked.
